text:
morgan: heads up - after flipping the fa3 kernels to canary on a subset of hosts we see an unexpected 8-12% p95 latency uplift on 8k-seq workloads. not across the board though, looks input-shape dependent :confused:
eli: saw this in perf lab too. only when batch_size <= 4 and seq >= 4k. larger batches look fine.
priya: curious if it's workspace fragmentation. memory accounting logs show more allocations around runtime::Workspace::grow().
ranjan: can you paste the allocator logs? also which build? we shipped the fa3 build with new allocator heuristic (defer_coalesce=true).
morgan: build sha: faf3-2026-03-02. snippet from node logs:
```
[2026-03-02T14:12:02Z] warn runtime: failed to reserve contiguous workspace, requested=1.1GB, avail_fragments=3, total_avail=1.3GB
[2026-03-02T14:12:02Z] info runtime: falling back to kernel=matmul_slice (fa2-compatible)
[2026-03-02T14:12:02Z] perf sample: p95_infer_ms=48.3 (fa3), fallback_p95=42.9 (fa2)
```
eli: that matches. cost of fallback to multiple matmul calls seems to spike latency for short batches because of kernel setup overhead.
priya: could quantization path be involved? we enable bf16->fp16 truncation for fa3 on that build. maybe mixed-precision math is changing memory layout and causing fragmentation.
devon: i ran a quick repro on a single GPU with stress tool. toggling "defer_coalesce" back to false removed the p95 uplift. so allocator interaction is highly suspect.
ranjan: thanks. two follow-ups: 1) is it reproducible in canary autoscaler (multi-node)? 2) do we see higher allocator churn in telemetry?
morgan: 1) canary cluster yes (3 hosts), 2) telemetry shows a 2x increase in workspace_grow ops per minute on the affected hosts.
eli: propose we add a telemetry tag when fallback happens (kernel_fallback_reason) and surface it on the kernel dashboard. quick patch: add fallback_reason enum and increment counter.
priya: agree. also want an experiment: keep fa3 kernels but force a compacting pass before large-seq requests. add config: 
```yaml
kernel_select:
  prefer: fa3
  precompact_on_seq_ge: 2048
  fallback: fa2
```
ranjan: precompact sounds heavy but OK for a canary. devon can you patch runtime to allow precompact per-request flag?
devon: will do, small change. also adding a per-request debug header x-rt-workspace-stats to emit fragment map for traces.
morgan: timeline? this week we should: 1) add fallback_reason telemetry (eli) 2) revert defer_coalesce on canary hosts or toggle off (ranjan) 3) deploy precompact experiment behind config (devon) 4) gather A/B for 48 hours.
eli: I can get the telemetry PR today.
priya: I'll prepare the eval harness to run synthetic 8k seq with small batches and capture exact kernel choices + latency buckets.
ranjan: I'll coordinate the canary toggle and rollback plan if p95 stays up after 24h.
devon: patch in review, will land by EOD. adding a short-circuit so precompact runs only when seq >= threshold to limit overhead.
morgan: thanks - one more note: please collect real request traces where fallback occurred and attach sample inputs to the ticket. we need to reproduce memory layout deterministically.
ops-bot: incident created: RT-3421 - fa3 canary p95 uplift (assigned: ranjan) :white_check_mark:
eli: grabbing initial dashboard panels now. will post link when ready. :mag_right:
priya: nice thread. if the allocator is the root cause we should consider a long-term refactor to the workspace freelist to avoid interleaved small allocations during attention kernels. file a follow-up RFC if we confirm.
morgan: agreed. i'll open the RFC stub after A/B results. thanks all. :thumbsup:
